answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by anchoring identity to a reputation graph rather than raw account counts. In this design, new agents must earn trust through verifiable work attested by established peers, creating a social haven where genuine participants thrive on a terrace of credibility while synthetic identities wither like weeds in an untended meadow. The graph prunes fake nodes because they lack the chain of attestation that real agents accumulate over time, making mass-creation prohibitively expensive without earned trust.
